questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For practical reasons I preferred an English-speaking country within the EU. For personal reasons I really love the Irish culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can't recommend Limerick enough!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy. UL sent us several mails before arrival and they were very fast at responding to queries.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are several "student villages" in dorm style with shared kitchen among 4/6 people and (often) own bathroom. The price of rent depended on the village.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Kitchen shared between 6 people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a bit expensive but definitely worth it. You also get free access to UL Sport Arena with gym and pool.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of my friends did not get on-campus accommodation but UL has a staff member who helped them find accommodation elsewhere

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We first had to choose our courses after the 2nd week, so we had a chance to try different things

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Webinar, reception and mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try a lot of different things before choosing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 2nd year and 4th year courses and the overall level was the same and sometimes a bit lower than KU. The biggest difference is that they are not as deep in theory at UL than KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More practical aspects and less people at lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Careers and Influence in Public Leadership, Comparative European Politics, International Organisations and Global Governance, Issues and Concepts of Development, Policy-making in the EU.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Careers and influence in Public Leadership which was a mix of OF and DAK.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of beer and travel

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and some products at the supermarket were less expensive than Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UL is famous for their clubs and societies - I think there are about 70 of them. Most of them only cost 5€ to sign up for.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many! In addition to all the clubs and societies, UL Global also hosted a lot of events for exchange/international students. The Library and Student Life Center also hosted weekly events for all students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I signed up for so many things so it depended on the week. I really enjoyed trying something very different so I signed up for fencing and archery. I also really enjoyed crafts, dance and kayak. A majority of exchange students signed up for OPC (Outdoor pursuits) to go on hikes, climb, run and more - so that is a great way to meet a lot of new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: One of my favourite trips was to Donegal where we rented a car and drove around for a weekend. I also really enjoyed Galway, Ring of Kerry and Derry.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Irish people are like extroverted Danish people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for clubs and societies

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture! I loved grabbing a pint in the evening after uni and listening to live music while playing cards

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Sign up for a new sport 
2. Be active in the introduction week - I met some of my best friends there
3. Remember to take breaks - it is easy to be overwhelmed by all the stuff to do

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Before you go on exchange, it is nice to reflect on what your goal is for the stay; Is it to improve academically, meet new people, travel as much as possible or something else?

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many great people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not spending too much money because of the "holiday" mentality.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
